subject: Archaeology
title: The Bronze Age Collapse
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Bronze Age Collapse usable.

hook.text: Around 1200 BCE, almost every great civilization in the eastern Mediterranean collapsed within a single generation.

buildup.text: The Hittites, Mycenaeans, Egyptians, Assyrians, and Canaanites all fell or weakened severely between 1250 and 1150 BCE.

discovery.text: Letters from the period describe mysterious 'Sea Peoples' raiding coastlines.

twist.text: No single cause has been proven. Drought, earthquakes, trade disruption, and internal revolts may all have combined.

climax.text: It was history's first systems collapse — interconnected societies that were too dependent on each other to survive.

punchline.text: An entire world order collapsed in one generation. It took 400 years to rebuild.

quiz.question: What made the Bronze Age Collapse so devastating?
options: A single massive earthquake destroyed every major city simultaneously
Interconnected societies were too dependent on each other — when one fell, all fell
A new religion spread rapidly and caused all kingdoms to abandon their capitals

details.summary: Around 1200 BCE, multiple Bronze Age civilizations collapsed within decades — Mycenaean Greece, the Hittite Empire, Ugarit, and New Kingdom Egypt weakened simultaneously. No single cause explains this systemic collapse, which may have involved invasions, drought, earthquakes, and trade disruption.
details.whyItMatters: The Bronze Age Collapse shows that interconnected civilizations can fail catastrophically. Understanding how cascading crises — climate, conflict, trade disruption — interact is directly relevant to modern global risks.
takeaways: Multiple civilizations collapsed around 1200 BCE simultaneously
Causes likely included invasions, drought, and trade disruption
Interconnected systems can fail through cascading crises

faq.question: Who were the Sea Peoples?
faq.answer: Egyptian records describe waves of attackers from across the Mediterranean who destroyed coastal cities. Their exact identity remains debated — possibly displaced populations from collapsing civilizations. They may have been both cause and symptom of the broader collapse.

faq.question: Did any civilizations survive the Bronze Age Collapse?
faq.answer: Egypt survived in weakened form. Assyria endured and eventually built a new empire. Some Phoenician cities maintained trade networks. But the interconnected palace economies of the eastern Mediterranean were destroyed, ushering in a centuries-long dark age across the region.
